accuracy.reason: Cards 1-3 correctly scope durable authority to the database, assign hit/miss/fill work to the API and distinguish result keys. Cards 4-6 avoid false freshness, TTL-residence or shared-cache synchronization guarantees.

evidence.quote: TTL limits an entry's lifetime, not the age of the source data used to fill it.

mechanisms.reason: Cards 2-4 trace hit/miss and the delayed old-fill race. Cards 5-7 explain expiration versus capacity removal, separate local copies, shared failure scope and coalescing/capped fallback. Inspected diagrams agree with API responsibility and stale database/cache divergence.

evidence.quote: A reader can fetch $20 before the update, pause, then refill $20 after removal.

coherence.reason: All eight objectives and declared dependencies progress from repeated work to paths, keys, updates, removal, placement, load failure and final choice. The learner transfers mechanisms to distinct scenarios without requiring a continuous story.

evidence.quote: Define what the key identifies, who fills it, and where the authoritative data lives.

decisions.reason: Cards 6-8 compare placement and failure scope, protect source capacity during outages, and reject caching low-reuse work. Card 4 places freshness-critical acceptance at authority; costs and measurable benefit guide choice.

evidence.quote: Falling back to the database is a load decision, not a free recovery path.

clarity.reason: Plain actor/action explanations and short price/key examples make the races and costs concrete without adding unnecessary implementation detail. Hit ratio, TTL, eviction and coalescing are defined when introduced.

evidence.quote: A hit avoids this database lookup. A miss still needs the database.

outcomes.reason: Connects repeated station-language reads to source-work savings; includes both key inputs, application-controlled hit/miss/fill and retained lookup/fill/source costs.
Correctly traces A restoring the old hours after deletion, rejects unconditional freshness and chooses authoritative bypass under the explicit database-read prerequisite.
Correctly classifies 12:03 stale hit, 12:11 expiration miss, 12:05 eviction miss; separates removal from refresh and lifetime from guaranteed residence or source freshness.

Chooses shared entry under no-concurrent-fill assumption, explains independent stale local copies, network versus in-process access, operational cost and one-instance versus all-instance cache-access failure.

Explains duplicate refill work and one in-progress fetch shared by readers. Outage response caps aggregate database work and rejects excess; optional stale result requires an independently available copy and respects 60 seconds.
Rejects cache-after-read for single-use keys, cites ample latency/capacity, added writes/storage/management and a relevant repeated-expensive-read or source-pressure reconsideration trigger.

sourceChecks.claim: Live inspected Azure caching guidance: repeated relatively static expensive reads are effective candidates; cache storage and access carry costs and the original source remains the data authority for this pattern.
Live inspected Azure cache-aside steps: application cache lookup, database fetch on miss, application fill and return. Presence does not establish source consistency.

Live inspected Azure explicit cache-aside code and structured key namespace guidance; result-varying inputs must distinguish reusable results. Private-result key isolation follows directly from avoiding reuse across different answers.

Live inspected cache-aside database-write then invalidation and explicit lack of consistency guarantee. Traced the supplied older-fetch/pause/delete/refill interleaving: deletion cannot cancel a later independent fill.

Live inspected Redis eviction policies: memory pressure can remove TTL keys early, LRU favors less recent use and noeviction rejects new writes. Azure TTL instructions remove keys after time; neither removal performs source reload.
Live inspected AWS local/external cache sections: independent processes may disagree, shared fleet reduces copies but adds a dependency and does not eliminate update failures.

Live inspected AWS thundering herd/request coalescing and cache-unavailability guidance: one pending source request reduces duplicates; load shedding, source caps and permitted stale data protect dependencies.
Live inspected Azure candidate conditions and AWS unique-per-request no-benefit case; measurable source cost, reuse and freshness govern whether the cache is justified.
